subject: BrightPay dedicated pool strain — urgent triage and exec visibility requested
messages:
From: BrightPay SRE <sre@brightpay.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-19T08:15:00Z
Subject: Dedicated pool pressure — 5xx spike and token queueing

Jonas,

We're seeing sustained degradation on our BrightPay reserved capacity for the last ~90 minutes. Key signals: average generation latency up ~3x (p95 ~2.2s -> 6.8s), 5xx rate rising to 4.8% (baseline <0.2%), and reserved throughput reporting a 28% headroom drop despite reservation intact. Queue depth for tokenization and KV lookups spiked concurrently.

Attached are a compacted logs bundle and a short KV cache dump. We think user-facing errors are coming from token queueing/backpressure rather than model timeouts, but the stack traces point to heavy tail on a few GPUs. Impact: several production customers intermittently seeing slow responses and occasional failures. BrightPay is on a paid reserved plan (deal BP-34722). We're holding a runbook stand-up but wanted to get Redwood eyes asap.

Attachments: [logs_20270419.tar.gz], [kvcache_dump.txt]

Can someone from infra/AM triage and propose immediate mitigations (routing, fallback, burst authorization)?

— Laura Chen
Director, Platform Reliability
BrightPay
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightPay SRE <sre@brightpay.com>, Laura Chen <laura@brightpay.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T08:24:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool pressure — 5xx spike and token queueing

Thanks Laura — looping in Marissa and Neha for immediate action.

Plan (short list):
- Marissa: please stand up a 30-min triage bridge and confirm customer-facing mitigation (temporary rate limit / fallback to hosted model).
- Neha: please check recent model/ rollout activity on the BrightPay dedicated pool (last 12 hours) and run a quick hot-rebalance of slabs if needed. Look at per-GPU tail latencies and KV cache miss patterns.
- I'll prep a brief for leadership if we need to request burst capacity or credits.

Please add any telemetry links. If this is a noisy neighbor, we'll aim for a pool isolate and reprovision plan.

Jonas
Account Exec — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: BrightPay SRE <sre@brightpay.com>, Laura Chen <laura@brightpay.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-19T08:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool pressure — 5xx spike and token queueing

Laura / BrightPay team — joining now. We're bringing up an ops bridge: https://meet.redwood.com/bridge/brightpay-20270419

Immediate mitigations we'll apply in the next 10-20 minutes (non-disruptive first):
- Enable per-route soft rate-limit (95th percentile) for non-critical endpoints to give headroom to core flows.
- Temporarily route a small percentage (~15%) of BrightPay traffic to a hosted model variant with identical behavior (cold fallback) to reduce pressure on the dedicated pool.
- Turn on increased KV cache prefetching to reduce on-the-fly miss spikes.

We need telemetry: route IDs, user patterns, and any recent model updates or config changes in the last 12 hrs. Laura — can you confirm whether you pushed any traffic pattern changes or batch jobs that might explain the spike?

I'll keep the BrightPay execs updated on the bridge outcome.

— Marissa Cole
Commercial Lead, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ops Oncall <ops-oncall@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightPay SRE <sre@brightpay.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T08:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool pressure — preliminary findings and proposed actions

Quick technical summary from the bridge:
- We see an abrupt increase in long-running KV lookup tasks pinned to 3 GPUs (IDs: g3,g7,g8) starting ~07:50Z; those GPUs show p99 latency > 12s and elevated CUDA contention.
- No config change in our rollout logs for BrightPay in the last 24 hrs, but we did complete an unrelated internal model alpha rollout to the same cluster earlier today (multi-tenant failure domain overlap). Likely noisy neighbor / packing inefficiency.
- There is a large background bulk convert job originating from one tenant that coincided with the spike (we've isolated the job ID).

Proposed immediate actions (engineering):
1) Scoped drain: evacuate requests off g3/g7/g8 to redistribute load (5-10 min ops window).
2) Pause the background bulk convert job (owner identified) and re-schedule off-peak.
3) Warm-cache on target hosts before traffic cutover.
4) If headroom still insufficient after redistribution, authorize a short-term burst to adjacent capacity and enable fallback routing for low-criticality endpoints.

I've attached a quick P99 graph and the per-GPU metrics extract. If Ops approves, I'll start the drain now.

Attachments: [p99_latency_graph.png]

— Neha Kapoor
Sr. SWE, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura@brightpay.com>, BrightPay SRE <sre@brightpay.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T09:05:00Z
Subject: Escalation: BrightPay reserved-capacity shortfall — decision requested within 1 hour

Priyom — flagging for visibility / authorization. BrightPay (BP-34722) is experiencing persistent latency and a rise in 5xx tied to dedicated pool saturation. Engineering (Neha) recommends a scoped drain + pause of a bulk job; if that does not restore headroom we should:

- Approve a temporary burst allocation (one-time) from adjacent capacity for up to 2 hours to avoid SLA hits, or
- Approve a one-off service credit in case we need a partial fallback for >30m of degraded service.

Customer impact: degraded response times for payment-sensitivity flows; risk of SLA credit if errors persist >60 minutes. We need a quick decision to proceed with the more invasive mitigations and to communicate timeline to BrightPay execs.

Suggested text for exec brief to BrightPay (I can send once you greenlight the action): short summary of root cause hypothesis, steps taken, timeframe to normalization (1-2 hours), and compensation/credits posture if we miss SLA.

Jonas
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura@brightpay.com>, BrightPay SRE <sre@brightpay.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-19T10:05:00Z
Subject: Update: actions taken and next steps (BrightPay dedicated pool)

Laura — update from the bridge and ops:
- Neha started a scoped drain of the three impacted GPUs and paused the identified bulk convert job. Early telemetry shows queue depth dropping and p95 latency trending back toward baseline.
- We also enabled a 15% hosted-model fallback for low-priority routes to preserve capacity for critical payment flows.
- Ops has requested short-term burst approval; Priyom is on the thread for a quick sign-off.

Timeline: we expect most user-facing errors to abate within 30-60 minutes; full normalization and verification across regions will take ~2 hours. We'll follow up with a post-incident note within 24 hours including root cause, remediation, and a proposed action to avoid co-location of noisy internal rollouts with reserved customer pools.

Attachments: [logs_20270419.tar.gz] (sanitized)

If you want a short exec note to circulate at BrightPay, I've drafted one and can share now.

— Marissa Cole
Commercial Lead, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
